1.pericope_label: Son of man, set thy face against Gog, the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him
debates: Who the enemy named here is
Whether the names belong to one person or to a class of enemies
Why the defeat is announced before the invasion
outliers: Wesley declines every single identification and takes the names for all the enemies of the people in every quarter, where Clarke narrows the field to two candidates
Ellicott grounds the name in the recent Scythian inroads the prophet would himself have remembered, rather than in any later ruler
themes: A king and a kingdom named together, as a ruler and his people
Hooks put into the jaws of an enemy to bring him where he is to fall
Assurance of deliverance given before the danger is even disclosed
A name left as a terror for fierce skill in war, cruelty and rapacity

3.pericope_label: And I will turn thee back, and put hooks into thy jaws, and I will bring thee forth, and all thine army
debates: Whether the turning back is a repulse or a leading out
Whether the allied nations are a literal confederacy or a symbol
Whether the command to prepare is ironic
outliers: Clarke alone reads the turning back as the failure of the enterprise, where Gill, Ellicott and Keil and Delitzsch all make it the drawing of the enemy toward his own destruction
Ellicott holds a literal alliance of nations so far apart to be out of the question, against Gill and Clarke who identify each name with a country on the map
themes: Hooks in the jaws, and fishes drawn out of the water
Nations summoned from the confines of the known world
Preparation commanded and then derided
Titles of greatness repeated to show they will not protect their bearer

8.pericope_label: After many days thou shalt be visited: in the latter years thou shalt come into the land that is brought back from the sword
debates: What being visited after many days means
How long the land had lain waste, and what that dates
Whether the three named peoples are allies or onlookers
outliers: Keil and Delitzsch reject an interpreter who took the key word to mean being missed or perishing, and hold to a penal visitation that includes the invasion itself
Ellicott argues from the word for continually that the desolation named is too long for the captivity and points to a later dispersion
themes: A whole career of sin spoken of as itself a visitation on the sinner
A land of unwalled villages, without bars or gates
A people living at the navel of the earth, rich and unsuspecting
Merchants who bargain for the spoil before the attack begins

14.pericope_label: Art thou he of whom I have spoken in old time by my servants the prophets of Israel
debates: Whether the question about knowing marks the inducement of the enemy or his disappointment
What earlier prophecies are appealed to
What the sanctifying of God in this enemy consists in
outliers: Ellicott argues that since no earlier prophecy now extant names this enemy, and none is likely to have been lost, the passage cannot relate to a particular event at all
Clarke reports two rival datings resting on identifications with a Syrian and a Persian king respectively, both of which Ellicott reasoning would exclude
themes: A small and undesigned occasion from which a great enterprise takes its rise
A people dwelling safely not in their own apprehension only but in reality
Wrath ascending into the face of God
A struggle between the powers of the world and the kingdom of God, prolonged through all prophecy

18.pericope_label: Thus will I magnify myself, and sanctify myself; and I will be known in the eyes of many nations
debates: Whether these verses quote older prophecies or are spoken now
Whose sword is called against the enemy
Whether the hail and fire are literal or figurative
outliers: Keil and Delitzsch reject two interpreters who took the verses for words spoken through the ancient prophets and only transferred here, arguing from the prophetic force of the perfect tense
Gill reads the particle as causal rather than as the sign of the object, making the verse give the reason for the shaking rather than name a new judgment
themes: Wrath ascending into the nose, as smoke from the nostrils of an angry man
Fishes of the sea trembling at a presence, not at an army
Swords of princes held at the command of God
Every man sword against his brother throughout the holy mountains
